patterns.title: Yoga Nidra
patterns.short_description: Let a guided sequence carry attention through body, breath, and experience while making room for rest.
use_when: A quiet break keeps turning into planning, scrolling, or checking whether you have relaxed.
You want a supported form of guided rest with few decisions to make.
You are interested in a resting contemplative practice without demanding a particular state.
goals: Make room for rest without requiring a performance of relaxation.
Explore receptive attention within a guided yogic practice.
mechanisms: Supported posture and externally supplied attentional structure; practical rationale rather than an established causal account.
Allowing sensations and thoughts without immediately correcting or interpreting them.
patterns.difficulty: Introductory guided forms; fit varies with the person and recording.
prerequisites: A setting where resting and possible drowsiness are safe.
Guidance whose pace, language, and invitations feel workable.
not_ideal_when: Driving or another responsibility requires sustained alertness.
Inward attention, imagery, or stillness increases panic, disconnection, or distress.
The intended use is to replace necessary sleep or assessment of persistent insomnia.
example_user_queries: I am exhausted but my mind keeps working when I lie down.
Every break turns into more scrolling and I do not feel rested.
Trying to relax just gives me another thing to get right.
I want a guided way to rest without having to organize an exercise myself.
My body is tired but I keep planning tomorrow.
I would like a quiet transition between work and the rest of my evening.
Can I rest even if I cannot make my mind go blank?
I keep checking whether meditation is working instead of settling into it.
Is falling asleep during a guided rest session a failure?
I want to understand how guided yogic rest differs from a body scan.

visual_decision.reason: Narrative examples explain the attentional move. A fixed-stage diagram would imply one universal sequence, and a sleep-stage graphic would overstate the evidence.

sources.title: Yoganidrā: An Understanding of the History and Context
sources.supports: Historical distinctions, Satyananda/Bihar lineage, and components of the modern guided method.

sources.title: The Effects of an Online Yoga Nidra Meditation on Subjective Well-Being and Diurnal Salivary Cortisol: A Randomised Controlled Trial
sources.authors: Esther N. Moszeik, Nicolas Rohleder, and Karl-Heinz Renner
sources.supports: Small, outcome-dependent psychological benefits; intervention variation and dropout limitations.

sources.title: Improved sleep, cognitive processing and enhanced learning and memory task accuracy with Yoga nidra practice in novices
sources.supports: Preliminary overnight sleep findings from a before-and-after pilot, without a parallel sleep control group.

sources.title: Electrophysiological Evidence of Local Sleep During Yoga Nidra Practice
sources.supports: Wake scoring during practice with some regional slow-wave activity; does not establish sleep replacement.

sources.title: Behavioral and psychological treatments for chronic insomnia disorder in adults: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline
sources.supports: Strong recommendation for multicomponent CBT-I for chronic insomnia in adults.

sources.title: Meditation and Mindfulness: Effectiveness and Safety
sources.authors: National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health
sources.supports: Meditation can involve negative experiences; this is broader meditation evidence, not a Yoga Nidra-specific adverse-event estimate.
